subject: english
question: What did many people expect when ATMs spread?

group.title: Reading comprehension
group.setup: Automation is usually discussed as a threat to jobs, but history suggests a more complicated picture. When automatic teller machines spread, many expected bank tellers to vanish. Instead, because each branch became cheaper to run, banks opened more branches, and tellers shifted from counting cash to selling products and solving problems. The lesson is not that technology never destroys work, for it plainly does, but that it changes which tasks are valuable. Workers who can move towards those tasks do well; those who cannot, or who are given no chance to learn, bear the cost of a progress that others enjoy.
